project-orkest.html.description: A shared interface language for business software, with CRM screens that make ownership, qualification and the next action easier to inspect.

project-hamro-idea.html.description: Connecting a Nepal-based studio's positioning, services, project proof and contact path in one maintainable website.

project-zakra-furniture.html.description: An image-led catalogue designed to remain coherent when real content replaces the demo.

blog/saas-dashboard-empty-state-ux-guide.description: Before writing an empty-state headline, identify what the interface actually knows. The next action should follow the cause, not a reusable illustration.

project-pihub.html.description: Financial workflows organized around what has been submitted, who needs to act and what remains unresolved.

project-yarsha.html.description: Keeping contact, asset selection and consequential actions understandable inside a conversational product.

project-zapp.html.description: Different interfaces for people booking a delivery, carrying it out and resolving exceptions around it.

project-morajaa.html.description: Helping a prospective client move from a recognizable business problem to a specific consulting service and a useful conversation.

project-masteriyo.html.description: Designing authoring and learning interactions inside an established LMS, while keeping the contribution boundary clear.

project-mokshya.html.description: A technical product story with an accessible first explanation and a deeper path for people evaluating the mechanism.

project-designerex.html.description: Balancing image-led fashion discovery with the stable rental information needed to compare listings.

project-splashnode.html.description: Explaining content, device and data-management capabilities through a website whose design and implementation can inform each other.

project-grid-labs.html.description: A hosting offer organized around service fit, plan comparison and a clear route to the next commercial step.

project-neverwinter-parser.html.description: Turning an event stream into an inspectable summary without making clean numbers look more certain than the underlying data.

project-sassboilerplate.html.description: A frontend learning archive of Sass imports and a Gulp build workflow, with attribution to JR Cologne’s original starter kit.

blog/ux-audit-evidence-before-redesign.h.description: A useful audit connects an observed problem to a task and a decision. Screenshots, analytics and opinions contribute different kinds of evidence; they should not be treated as interchangeable.

blog/ux-audit-checklist-before-redesign..description: Use this checklist to inspect one important journey from entry to recovery. A page-by-page visual review can miss the behavior that makes the task succeed or fail.

blog/prioritize-ux-audit-findings-before.description: A long issue list becomes useful when the team can explain why one problem deserves attention before another. Separate user consequence, evidence confidence and delivery effort.

blog/when-startup-needs-ux-audit-before-.description: A redesign is a commitment to change. An audit is useful when the team first needs to understand which change is warranted and which existing behavior should be preserved.

blog/beautiful-interface-poor-ux.html.description: A polished screen can still leave the person unsure what to do, what changed or whether their work is safe. Review the decision the interface supports before judging the composition.

blog/saas-dashboard-ux-checklist.html.description: A dashboard should help someone notice what matters and act on it. Use this checklist to review one role's work, not to collect every chart and table pattern in one screen.

blog/website-ux-checklist-software-compa.description: A software website should help a serious visitor understand the offer, inspect relevant proof and choose a sensible next step. Review that journey before adding another visual effect.

blog/blog-design-systems-front-end.html.description: A design system becomes useful when its concepts survive implementation. I look for clear responsibilities between tokens, components, content and product behavior.

blog/design-systems-small-product-teams..description: A small team needs a reliable way to repeat and change decisions. It does not need to reproduce the operating model of a much larger organization.

blog/blog-service-websites.html.description: A service page needs to help someone recognize their situation, understand the scope and decide whether a conversation is worthwhile. A list of capabilities is only the starting material.

blog/blog-portfolio-product.html.description: I want a portfolio to help someone evaluate my judgment, not only recognize a visual style. That means treating evidence, navigation and performance as part of the same product.

blog/blog-gaming-interface-clarity.html.description: Playing complex games and working on a combat-data tool keeps bringing me back to the same interface question: can I tell what matters now, and can I inspect why?

blog/hire-product-designer-nepal-saas-we.description: Evaluate the work against your product's decisions, collaboration needs and evidence gaps. Location is one practical consideration; it should not substitute for examining the contribution.

blog/blog-web3-products.html.description: Start with what the person is trying to do. Explain the wallet or network when it changes the decision, instead of making protocol vocabulary the entrance requirement.

blog/web3-wallet-connection-ux.html.description: Wallet connection should answer why the wallet is needed, what is being requested and how to continue if the person declines or cannot connect.

blog/transaction-review-ux-crypto-apps.h.description: A transaction review should help someone understand the change they are about to authorize. It should also be honest about what the product can and cannot establish before submission.

blog/web3-wallet-ux-checklist.html.description: Review the whole journey: explanation, connection, intent, authorization, waiting, recovery and the result. A successful connection is only one checkpoint.

blog/figma-handoff-notes-for-developers..description: A useful handoff note answers the questions the image cannot: what changes, what persists and what happens when the action does not work.

blog/blog-good-handoff.html.description: Handoff is a shared understanding of the product decision. Exporting a polished screen is one part of it, not the point at which responsibility disappears.

blog/design-handoff-checklist-startup-pr.description: A small team needs enough agreement to build safely, without turning every change into a specification project. Use this checklist for a release slice, not the entire product at once.

blog/responsive-saas-dashboard-handoff-n.description: A responsive dashboard needs rules for priority, overflow and continuation. A desktop frame and a mobile frame leave the hardest decisions between them.

blog/saas-dashboard-filter-ux.html.description: A filter changes the answer a table gives. People need to see the question currently being asked, understand why a record is absent and change that question without losing context.

blog/role-based-saas-dashboard-ux.html.description: Role-based UX is not a reason to duplicate every screen. Share the meaning of a record and its states, then change the information and actions according to the job.

blog/saas-dashboard-empty-states-product.description: A product needs an empty-state model before it needs an empty-state component. Visually similar panels can represent different responsibilities and different risks.

blog/saas-dashboard-empty-states-that-he.description: An empty state is useful when someone can continue from it. Test the transition, retained input and result of the recovery action, not only the appearance of the panel.
